name: Marqeta, Inc.

profile.description: Marqeta (Oakland, CA; founded 2010) runs a modern, API-based card-issuing platform, acting as issuer processor and card program manager for fintechs, BNPL providers and expense-management companies [3]. CEO Mike Milotich, previously CFO, was confirmed as CEO in September 2025 after a seven-month interim period [5]. Q2 2026 net revenue was $176.0M (+17% YoY) on total processing volume of ~$120B (+32%), GAAP net income was $8M and Adjusted EBITDA $37M (+31%); 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $699.9M-$706.1M and a $150M buyback was authorized in August 2026 [1][2].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Marqeta's configurable card-issuing platform has extended into card program management alongside issuer processing, an incremental extension of the original product rather than a new revenue engine [3]. AI Deployment (1/2): The company hired former Capital One ML VP Fouzi Husaini as Chief AI Officer in September 2024 and has shipped Marqeta Docs AI and AI-driven risk decisioning for real-time fraud prevention, but no quantified AI revenue or savings are disclosed [6]. Market Share (1/2): TPV grew 33% in Q1 2026 to $112B and ~32% in Q2 to ~$120B, well above revenue growth, implying share gains in modern issuing, but no market-share data was found [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Guidance gives Q3 revenue of $173.1-$176.4M and FY2026 revenue of $699.9-$706.1M, but no named next-generation products with launch dates [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP data shows R&D at only 2.5% of revenue on a TTM basis (technology costs are mostly reported elsewhere), so above-average intensity cannot be shown [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Marqeta articulates a clear purpose around modernizing card issuing and has published its cultural principles ('The Marqeta Way'), but the mission is product-descriptive rather than a deeper purpose [3][7]. Community Impact (0/2): No company foundation or quantified community programs surfaced in research. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found; leadership has turned over repeatedly (interim CEO from February 2025), and Comparably respondents rate the executive team only C+ [5][6]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show one open-market purchase against 35 reported sales over the last four quarters [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock. Strengths: debt-to-equity of 2.2% (1.0) with ~$9.12 of cash per share, TTM revenue growth of 22.4% (1.0) and an FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 16.6% (1.0, 2x weight) [4]. Weaknesses: ROE is only 1.4% (0.09, 2x weight), net margin is 1.5% (0.08), the derived forward P/E of 35.4x on FY2027 consensus EPS of $0.51 scores 0.61, and FMP's forward PEG of -0.70 is negative and scores 0 (2x weight) [4]. Weighted sum 4.87/10 rounds to 5. Liquidity (~$16M daily traded value) clears the floor. Note the 5-year revenue CAGR is flattered by the 2023 Cash App contract restructuring that changed revenue presentation, so growth comparisons across years are imperfect.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Marqeta's core is regulated payments infrastructure (issuer processing on Visa/Mastercard rails, bank-sponsor relationships, compliance) that AI tools cannot readily replicate, and AI-driven agentic commerce still needs card credentials to transact, which is a potential demand tailwind [3][6]. Points are withheld because AI lowers the cost of building payments software, which could intensify competition from larger processors and in-house builds, and no analyst commentary was found that rules out that pressure. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI products (Docs AI, AI risk decisioning) are shipping but no AI revenue figure is disclosed [6].

infinite_game.summary: Viewed as Simon Sinek would, Marqeta is still a finite player: a talented platform whose story is told in TPV, Adjusted EBITDA and buyback authorizations, governed through a period of founder-control disputes and three CEO transitions in roughly two years. The technology could anchor a lasting cause around open, programmable money movement, but leadership has not yet articulated or tested one.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Marqeta's purpose of modernizing card issuing is real but reads as a product description; no future-state vision is visible in leadership's communication, which centers on revenue guidance, EBITDA growth and a $150M repurchase plan [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Investing in a dedicated Chief AI Officer and AI fraud tooling while the company was still GAAP-unprofitable shows some willingness to fund long-term capability [6]. But capital is also flowing to buybacks, and a December 2024 securities class action alleges management understated regulatory headwinds before a guidance cut that sent the stock down ~42.5% [8].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Leadership has been unstable, with the founder departing, a 2023 Delaware suit over a buyback that risked giving the founder control, and an interim CEO from February 2025 [5][8]. Comparably respondents rate overall culture 4.2/5 but the executive team only C+, a sign of limited trust in leadership [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Marqeta has moved from pure issuer processing toward full card program management and has absorbed a major restructuring of its largest customer relationship, showing adaptive capacity, though not a cause-driven reinvention [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found framing competitors such as Adyen, Galileo or Stripe Issuing as rivals to learn from; communications focus on volume and profitability metrics [1][2].

investment_thesis: Marqeta is finally profitable on a GAAP basis, with Q2 2026 net income of $8M, Adjusted EBITDA of $37M (+31% YoY) and TPV of ~$120B growing 32%, and FY2026 revenue guided to $699.9-$706.1M [1][2]. The balance sheet is a fortress (D/E 2.2%, ~$9.12 cash per share against an $18.07 price) and the stock trades at ~10x price-to-free-cash-flow with a 9.8% FCF yield, while a $150M buyback authorization covers ~9% of the market cap [4][2]. Consensus models EPS rising from $0.23 in 2026 to $1.00 by 2030 [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case: revenue growth (+17% in Q2) is decelerating well below TPV growth, FY2026 guidance was narrowed below estimates, and net margin is just 1.5% with ROE of 1.4%, so profitability is fragile [2][4]. Stock-based compensation runs at ~13.9% of revenue, a December 2024 securities class action remains a governance overhang, and repeated leadership turnover weighs on execution [4][8]. On the IOWN framework, weak Inspiration (2/10) and a FINITE Infinite Game score (3/10) hold the overall at 41, a WATCH.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November): delivery within the $173.1-$176.4M revenue guide and continued 30%+ TPV growth would ease concern over the narrowed full-year outlook [2]
Execution of the $150M share repurchase authorized August 3, 2026, roughly 9% of the current market cap, at a ~10x free-cash-flow multiple [1][4]
Commercialization of AI-driven risk decisioning and agentic-commerce card credentials, which could open a measurable AI revenue line under Chief AI Officer Fouzi Husaini [6]
key_risks: Take-rate compression: revenue growth of ~17% trails TPV growth of ~32%, indicating pricing pressure or mix shift toward lower-yield clients [2]
Regulatory exposure: the December 2024 securities class action alleges understated regulatory challenges after a guidance cut drove a ~42.5% one-day drop [8]
Thin profitability: 1.5% TTM net margin and 13.9% SBC-to-revenue leave little cushion if volume growth slows [4]
